Comments (English): I am a meticulous buyer who reads reviews and searches before buying, so I wrote a detailed review since I received this from Coupang~ Final comment We are a two-person household, and we like to cook and eat a lot of home-cooked meals, so there are quite a few dishes to wash even after eating one meal~ Since the dishwasher works so hard, I don’t have to worry about washing the dishes while eating! This is why I think it’s great for my aunts. I now have time to enjoy other hobbies while washing the dishes~! Reason for selection One of the three dishwashers for my aunts~ I’ve never used one before. I was worried that I would not use it or that it would be inconvenient after installing it~ But I gained courage since I didn’t have to install or drill any holes for the 3-person one~ Since it’s so convenient, should I give it a try? The media dishwasher had good reviews~ So I tried it~ Design I prefer white electric products, but the option is black, but it didn't look stuffy because it's black on white~ It's also easy to press because it's touch-type^^ Size It's a little bigger than the oven-type air fryer in my house~ I measured the size to see if it would fit my kitchen, and the width was roomy, and the height was just right for the small TV panel in my kitchen~ I chose it because the size was just right! It will be helpful if you check the width, length, and height carefully before purchasing~ Important way to put in water Since it's non-installable, you have to put in water separately~ 1. Turn on the power first so that it recognizes the water level! 2. Pour 5L of water with the enclosed water cup~ 3. Since it's a 1.8L cup, if you put in 1.8L+1.8L+1.4L, it makes a beeping sound when it's full of water~ Then stop putting in water! If you put in water without turning on the power first, it may not recognize it and may damage the product, so you have to follow this order! Five stars. How to use the course Wash the larvae, put them in the dishwasher, and select the washing course~ Standard: 64 minutes, wash 65, rinse 70, dry, power consumption 0.4kWh, water usage 5L Powerful: 81 minutes, wash 65, rinse 72, dry, power consumption 0.5kWh, water usage 5L Eco: 80 minutes, wash 50, rinse 65, dry, power consumption 0.3kWh, water usage 5L Rapid: 29 minutes, wash 55, rinse 60, dry, power consumption 0.27kWh, water usage 5L Steam sterilization: 64 minutes, wash 50, rinse 72, dry, power consumption 0.4kWh, water usage 5L Since the water usage is 5L in total, you can select the course according to the purpose~ I used standard or rapid~ Those who use bottles can use steam sterilization. It was the same~ After using it, the cleaning power is really good~ I wondered how well the machine could do the things I used to do by hand, such as washing and cleaning. It's really good! There's a program that dries after washing, and even if you don't go out or open the door, the fan will run for 72 hours, so it seems better than a dishwasher that turns off! However, after using it, I wish there was a separate course that only dries~ It doesn't dry well, so it's a little disappointing for me who doesn't want to leave even a single drop of moisture~ And it makes some noise when water is put in or drained~ I was a little surprised at first~~ So I don't recommend running the dishwasher too early or too late! However, after using it, it was so good that I can install it and use it without any burden, and it seems much better than buying an expensive brand-name product~ I recommend it! Sentence (English): We are a family of four raising one kindergartener and one elementary school student.
Comments (English): We are a family of four raising one kindergartener and one elementary school student. Initially, I was looking for a mini dishwasher, but I decided to look for a slightly larger size, which led me to this product that is drill-free and easy to move. First off, it is excellent in terms of usability. I use it at least once a day, and sometimes even twice when there are a lot of dishes. The size is just right for a family of four to wash the dishes generated after meals. It has made it much easier to clean the kids' water bottles and dishes, which are a hassle to wash every day. Also, having a dishwasher has reduced the burden of taking out various cooking utensils when preparing meals. I am currently using liquid detergent and am satisfied with it. However, if dishes overlap, those parts sometimes don't get cleaned properly. So, I am trying my best to arrange them like Tetris so they don't overlap as much as possible. Also, this product has a door-opening feature once the wash is finished, so I really love that I can leave it running and go out with peace of mind. If the door doesn't open, moisture gets trapped inside for hours, which makes a full wash worse than not washing at all. I am very satisfied with the door opening feature. I mainly use two functions: the 1 hour 40 minute course for heavy grease and the 50 minute course for general use. It definitely seems like the 1 hour 40 minute course cleans things more thoroughly, though that might just be my imagination. Based on my personal experience using it for a month, this is a dishwasher I really want to recommend to everyone around me! Lately, whenever I meet people, I go around recommending it to them, telling them they absolutely must buy a dishwasher. I am using it well. I hope you create and release even better products in the future.

Sentence (English): I am using it well.
Comments (English): We are a family of four raising one kindergartener and one elementary school student. Initially, I was looking for a mini dishwasher, but I decided to look for a slightly larger size, which led me to this product that is drill-free and easy to move. First off, it is excellent in terms of usability. I use it at least once a day, and sometimes even twice when there are a lot of dishes. The size is just right for a family of four to wash the dishes generated after meals. It has made it much easier to clean the kids' water bottles and dishes, which are a hassle to wash every day. Also, having a dishwasher has reduced the burden of taking out various cooking utensils when preparing meals. I am currently using liquid detergent and am satisfied with it. However, if dishes overlap, those parts sometimes don't get cleaned properly. So, I am trying my best to arrange them like Tetris so they don't overlap as much as possible. Also, this product has a door-opening feature once the wash is finished, so I really love that I can leave it running and go out with peace of mind. If the door doesn't open, moisture gets trapped inside for hours, which makes a full wash worse than not washing at all. I am very satisfied with the door opening feature. I mainly use two functions: the 1 hour 40 minute course for heavy grease and the 50 minute course for general use. It definitely seems like the 1 hour 40 minute course cleans things more thoroughly, though that might just be my imagination. Based on my personal experience using it for a month, this is a dishwasher I really want to recommend to everyone around me! Lately, whenever I meet people, I go around recommending it to them, telling them they absolutely must buy a dishwasher. I am using it well. I hope you create and release even better products in the future.

Comments (English): [ Product review ] || ---------------- || Overall, I would have to say that I have been extremely pleased with my new dishwasher. I do, however, have a few issues. My main objection to this configuration arises from the fact that I am forced to load my utensils handle side down. I know that I can shift the grid, but that results in an open space and I am unable to load as many utensils. I am slowly adapting to the other differences. The machine does an excellent job of cleaning – sometimes too good a job! When I washed my hot beverage container, the machine started to remove the plastic coating. Needless to say, I will not make that mistake again. All in all, I am very happy that we chose to purchase your product and I am recommending it to my friends.

Sentence (English): It cleans the dishes well and it is very quiet.
Comments (English): [ Cleans well but not worth the high price ] || ---------------- || It cleans the dishes well and it is very quiet. The silverware holder is very small, half the size of any other dishwasher. We're using the one from our last dishwasher. The machine stays wet inside, even after the dishes are removed and it's empty for a day, the entire back stays wet. I have to leave the door open for it to dry. You can't open the door partialy, it won't stay, it has to be fully opened with the door near the floor so it's a tripping hazard. After trying 3 different loads, we tried the Crystal Dry option and that finally worked and the machine was dry inside. That doesn't make sense to me, if that's the only way the machine will dry, then why isn't it just standard, why do you have to chose that as an extra option? The racks are not smooth rolling, you have to use force to pull them out and push them back in. There are just a few options on the dishwasher, but they offer many options if you use the App. I wouldn't have purchased this machine if I realized that's what it was. I thought the option on the App was if you wanted to start it from outside the home. When I'm done loading the machine, I want to quickly and easily push the buttons, start the machine, and walk away. I don't want to have to use my phone to pick the extra options or cycles that aren't on buttons on the machine. I would return this machine if they would take it back.

Comments (English): [ Excellent features ] || ---------------- || We chose this model so we could install a cabinet door panel on it to match the rest of our kitchen. The installation directions are a little confusing -- the manual says to make sure to install the dishwasher first, and the panel installation guide says to make sure to install the cabinet panel first. You're supposed to call their support line if your panel isn't within that range. We've been using this dishwasher for about a month now. The dishwasher is really incredibly quiet during operation. The "Auto" cycle is long (2:39), which is normal these days for dishwashers, but the "Eco" cycle, for light loads, is just 1:25, which is a nice option. The middle drawer comes out half-way and then, due to a feature of being able to raise or lower the drawer to different heights, has to be yanked out pretty hard to come out the rest of the way. Same difficulty sliding it back in. That's the part I like least about this dishwasher. I used this same model during a trip to an AirBnB in England. A few of the bottom drawer rollers had broken off over time, which made it pretty difficult to roll in. They needed to buy new rollers. I'll keep an eye on mine, but hopefully they'll last several years.

Sentence (English): I love the dishwasher, but had some trouble getting it installed.
Comments (English): I love the dishwasher, but had some trouble getting it installed. It needed an extension kit, which was not included, so the first installer to arrive could not complete the job. The next installer who came opened the box and we saw a big dent in the front of the dishwasher. The third installer who came after a replacement was received refused to install becausehe said it required plumbing expertise. Finally got it installed on October 11 by Juan Ciprian, who did a great job. The online support for this product was great, and I was always able to get someone on the phone to reschedule the installation. I was unaware that the location of my dishwasher (not adjacent to the sink) might be a problem. Maybe this issue could be explored at the point of sale, so that appropriate supplies and installers could be scheduled.

Comments (English): [ Almost good ] || ---------------- || My new Kitchen Aid dishwasher does pretty much what I would expect, no more, no less. If I wash dishes right away after a meal, everything gets clean, but I had hoped that it would be strong and efficient enough that I could put a few days of dishes (hand-rinsed) in it before washing and they would all get clean. But alas, such is not the case. Most of it gets clean, but in each load there will always be several pieces of flatware, and a few glasses and dishes that don't come clean. So I have to wash them by hand. I have not tried a process of putting unrinsed dishes in the washer and rinsing them each night, before accumulating enough to wash after 2 or 3 days. I'm afraid the rinse cycle will use too much water. I do like the flatware tray at the top of the washer. I can remove the flatware basket on the bottom rack, and that gives me more room for dishes and pots and bowls.

Sentence (English): Purchased from Lowes in late 2022 (it is now late 2023) mostly because we have stayed with Whirlpool or Kitchenaid appliances for the last 40 years and have had great experiences with all appliances.
Comments (English): [ Great Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Purchased from Lowes in late 2022 (it is now late 2023) mostly because we have stayed with Whirlpool or Kitchenaid appliances for the last 40 years and have had great experiences with all appliances. This dishwasher does not disappoint. It is quiet and the racks seem to be well designed. The top tray for flatware is a nice feature. Everything has come out crystal clear so far using Cascade Platinum Pods and Finish rinse aid. When Lowes rep told us it would be about 2 weeks to have it installed, we decided to have a shot at installing it. It was delivered the next day and my spouse and I installed it ourselves. It took about 3 hours but we did it. Attaching and feeding power, drain tube and supply line around the back of the sink is not for the faint of heart! (Not to mention the black mold and an old piece of linoleum made with asbestos in the flooring we found after removing the old unit. Oye)

Sentence (English): I really like this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher so far. ] || ---------------- || I really like this dishwasher. It is elegant, capacious. Has lots of features and is QUIET. Setting is up the first time took a bit of doing because it has reservoirs for salt (to help with hard water), as well as rinse aid, and I had to learn how to set up or disable these features as needed. It was also a bit of a pain to set it up. In the app (to connect to WiFi). I do not like devices that call home but I set it up in a separate wifi network so no snooping . Once it connected though, it worked fine. It immediately downloaded an update and applied it itself. The app is a bit sluggish and not great to look at, but it does the job. My only gripe so far is that after the Auto cycle it leaves behind a lot of moisture. Not in the dishes themselves but on the door and insides. I'm pretty sure this can be remedied by increasing the drying time, which I will try next time. If that works, I will set up a FAVORITE washing profile so it can be a one-button preset from them on. I cannot speak as to reliability as I have only owned it for about 10 days, but given the price and the good reviews, I hope it will last me a long time.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.
