Sentence (English): This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day.
Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Sentence (English): This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day.
Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Sentence (English): I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte?
Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.
