Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. Sentence (English): Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made.
Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. There was water in the dented areas, and some were dry. I just left it as it was to dry. There was no need to take it out. Before buying a dishwasher, I was worried because it was so hot. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Comments (English): Ordered on 11/3, remodeled on 11/4, delivered on 11/9. I am using it right after installation. Since the oven space fits the specifications, I put the dishwasher in, so there was no remodeling cost, and the remodeling team took out the oven, and the dishwasher installation team came and picked it up free of charge. When it first starts? You can hear a hissing sound, and after that, the operating sound is not audible. You have to get right in front of it to hear the sound of water running. The operating method is easily marked, and I was worried because I thought it wouldn't work on plastic or glass, but it works with standard wash or glass wash mode? I put *thick glass* soy sauce paper in the standard wash mode and there was no problem. The glass wash mode is for thin glass? I think that's the only thing that applies. If you set it to standard mode, it just dries naturally, but you can also select the strong drying menu as an option, which is nice. The strong drying is also a natural drying, but when it opened automatically and I put my hand in, it was really hot. It dries faster than the standard mode because of the heat. It's not a hot air dryer. That's a different, latest model. The sterilization wash and strong drying modes go up to 75 degrees, so it's better not to put plastic in when selecting the two menus. This model 8065 has two baskets, so it's the perfect size for a household of three to wash dishes once a day. The other model, 8075, has three baskets, but it seems like it has advantages and disadvantages because of its height. Also, since I only use the menus that I use, and the price is also that, since I live with three people, I think 8065 is enough for me, so I bought this. If I hadn't bought the 12-person one, I think it would have been the same. Except for the plates, most of them have to be turned over, so even if there aren't many dishes to wash, it takes up a lot of space in the dishwasher. Since we have a baby, there's a lot of dishes to wash. I chose Kota White because I thought it would be white, but the color is matte? Light gray. It's too dark to call white. It's still pretty. Our kitchen sink is ivory, but it's a little yellow? A color that looks a little old and yellow? That's the original color, but I was worried that the color wouldn't go well, so I was worried until the day it arrived. Maybe because it's bespoke. It goes well with any color. I think it's pretty. Since it's a product that can be freestanding, the top is removed and installed. I'll give you the top in case you want to use it freestanding later. They said that the bolt that connects the top to the main machine is installed behind the main machine. I don't think you can put knives in it. The blades might touch the basket, so I think it might damage the basket? I'm a little worried. The rice cooker that had the rice stuck to it was washed well with the standard course, but when I put a spatula that had a little bit of an egg stuck to it, it wasn't cleaned well with the standard course. I think I'll have to select the steam soaking option to clean the stuck-on part. When it's finished, a very short melody plays and the door opens automatically. When it's finished with the standard course, is it hot? Warm? It's not enough to cause a moderate burn, but I think it dries naturally because of the heat. It seems to have washed well for now. I think I need to use it more to know. After using it for a week, I'm just spinning everything except the glass and knife. The glass is in the menu selection, but I thought it was a waste to just spin it for glass cleaning, so I just washed it by hand and spun it. When the door opens automatically, it dries naturally. I spun it around 9 pm and it took around 11 am the next day to dry naturally. When I took it out early in the morning around 8 am, some of the dishes were wet. Would it break quickly? Would it be easy to clean? Would it be hygienic? But I was so sick from washing dishes that I couldn't even touch my baby because my hands got eczema. So I made a decision, but now I have more time, and I can do other things with that time, and I feel better. I think this is a good purchase for me. I use less water than when I wash it. I don't usually look at the manual, but I think I should read the manual carefully at least once. It explains the menu selection, temperature, and how to place the dishes with pictures. Buy it when you get a card discount. It's different for each product. Even though the color is different, the card discount rate is different. I saw that the Kota White product was up to 15%. I've been using it for a month and it's working fine. I was very suspicious of the machine, so I watched it with an eagle eye. I really bought it for 12 people. If you have a family of 4 and a lot of dishes, you might feel it's small. Since the pot goes in, it takes up a lot of space. If you don't put the pot in, the space is wide. But since it's small, I put everything in. I put in the knife, glass, and everything in standard mode and turn it on. Instead, I don't put in the wine glass. Of all the things I've bought, this dishwasher is the best purchase I've ever made. My husband is very satisfied with it. I'm using it after 7 months. What I find a little inconvenient is that there is no proper place to put knives or scissors, so I put them between bowls with the blade facing upwards. I wonder if the blades will damage the basket. If it had been a three-tiered model, it would have been more convenient because there would have been an additional dedicated basket on top, but the price difference is significant and it takes up more space, so there are restrictions on putting tall pots and such underneath, so it was a bit of a problem. If I were to buy it again, I think I would buy a two-tier model. If the price difference were not significant, I would consider buying it, but other than that slight inconvenience, I am very satisfied.

Sentence (English): My old dishwasher broke down just a few days before Chuseok.
Comments (English): [ I like that the dishes are washed cleanly and the door opens automatically. ] || ---------------- || My old dishwasher broke down just a few days before Chuseok. I debated whether to buy a new one since my sink area is small, but I ended up not buying one. However, as I kept doing the dishes due to holiday food and the break, my fingers started hurting and I began to regret my decision. So, I started searching diligently for a dishwasher. I chose this model because I liked the price and it features an automatic door opening. I was worried about the pink color and whether it might look tacky, but I am very satisfied after installation. As a family of four, we wash dishes frequently even when we eat simply; this dishwasher cleans thoroughly, the door opens automatically, the design is sleek, and the bright pink color has made the kitchen look much prettier. The installation technician explained everything very kindly. If I do a quick pre-wash before putting the dishes in, they come out cleaner and fluffier than when I washed them myself. Although it is a single-tier unit, it is deep enough to fit all the dishes, and I can even put a pot on top to run it. I put in about 1/4 of a solid detergent packet, and it comes out perfectly clean. I hope I can use this Samsung dishwasher for a long time without any breakdowns.
Comments (Original): [ 그릇도 깨끗하게 세척되고 자동문열림이라서 좋아요. ] || ---------------- || 하필 추석 며칠전 s*세척기가 고장나서 이거 사야하나 씽크대도 좁은데 그냥 있을까 고민하다 그만 안 샀어요.명절음식이랑 연휴로 인해 설거지를 계속하며손가락이 아프고 후회를 하다가 식기세척기를 열심히 찾아보았어요.가격도 마음에 들고 자동문열림도 되는 이 제품으로 골랐어요. 근데 핑크라 어떨지 촌스러우면 어쩌지 했는데 설치하고 너무 만족합니다. 4인식구라 간단하게 먹어도 자주하게 되는데 설겆이도 깨끗하게 잘 되고 자동문열림이라 알아서 열려 있고 디자인도 깔끔하고 핑크색도 환해서 주방이 예뻐졌어요.설치기사님이 설명을 친절하게 잘 해 주시네요.애벌세척 간단하게 하고 넣어주면 제가 직접한거보다 더 깨끗하고 뽀송해져 있네요.1단이지만 깊어서 그릇이 다 들어가고 그위에 냄비도 하나 넣고 돌릴수 있어요. 고체세제 1/4정도 넣고 돌리니까 깨끗하게 되네요.삼성식기세척기 고장없이 오래 쓸수 있으면 좋겠어요.

We will have to see if it will last as long as my old kitchenaid dishwasher that is over 16 years old.

Comments (English): [ Fits our needs pretty well ] || ---------------- || Purchased this item in September. Delivery was fairly smooth, although the installer did not ensure the screws securing the dishwasher to the counter were flush which resulted in small "gashes" on the top of the door (where the settings are). Disappointing but not worth arguing about. In my opinion, the dishwasher utensil basket is too big and takes up too much room - it should be the type with detachable ends to make it smaller if needed. It was advertised to hold up to 12 or 14 place-settings, however I'm not so sure about that. Interior room is definitely less than my previous dishwasher of the same size. Also, personally I would have liked the controls on the outside of the dishwasher (like my previous one) since it is easier to tell how far along in the cycle you are and when the cycle is complete. I think there are probably better options available, however it's hard to complain with the price I paid on the Whirlpool site.

Sentence (English): Bought this to replace my GE that died after 17 years.
Comments (English): [ WORST Dishwasher EVER ] || ---------------- || Bought this to replace my GE that died after 17 years. This dishwasher has been a nightmare since day 1. Delivery and installation team required separate appointments, but installers won't take old dishwasher back, so I had to have it uninstalled myself prior to delivery or I was going to have to dispose of it myself. First delivery appointment was a no show, so I was stuck with a dead dishwasher in my living room for 2 weeks. Install was botched - the kid could not figure out how to get it installed and a separate appointment was set up with a more senior tech. After it was finally installed, I ran the dishwasher overnight and I woke up to water all over the floor. Installers came back out and determined it was a faulty unit, so I had to order a replacement from Costco. I had to have the faulty unit uninstalled prior to that delivery as well. Second unit was delivered, but there were no delivery appointments available. Huh? Costco gave me a $150 credit to hire someone else. I ended up having to pay $250. I should be happy now, right? Turns out this machine is a complete piece of crap. The ONLY good thing I can say is that it is quiet, but it does NOT clean the dishes! I like to run my dishwasher overnight because my electricity is cheaper after midnight. If there is even one speck of food on a dish or flatware, it is still on after the cycle completes. It's as if the water jets never get inside a glass or to the top 3rd rack at all. Samsung has sent repair persons out multiple times. Nearly every part of this machine has been replaced. It still doesn't clean. Samsung tried to tell me that my hot water has to be at LEAST 120 degrees for cycle to be effective, as there is no heating element in the unit. I pointed out there HAS to be a heating element in the unit because it has a SANITIZE cycle. Then they told me the problem was with my tankless water heater because a tankless heater requires several seconds of "draw" before kicking in, and then it takes 20-30 seconds to draw the hot water up from the unit in the basement. Because the dishwasher does not use a lot of water, it stops drawing water before the hot water gets to the unit. Ugh. Let's move on, cause there is more bad news. Flaw #1: The middle rack has 2 settings: high and low. If it is set to high, there is not enough height to put even a short wine glass in the 2nd rack. If it is set to low, I cannot put a full size dinner plate in the lower rack (I do not have oversized dishes). Flaw #2: The spacing and shape of the tines in the 2nd rack are very awkward. It's OK for most plain mugs and glasses, but oversized mugs, small dishes, lids, and plasticware either don't fit at all, or they take up 2 rows. Flaw #3: the many of the tines in the 2nd rack are spaced so far apart, that small lids or dishes consistently fall through. Flaw #4: Spacing of tines on bottom rack are also off. Pics on the Samsung website show plates in each slot, but customer service told me I had to skip every other slot so that water could get through. Huh? So I can only fill it halfway? Just in case you were wondering, it STILL doesn't clean when I skip every other slot. Every single time I look at that stupid $1k appliance, I get angry and regret the purchase. Worst money I have EVER spent on an appliance. Will NEVER buy Samsung again.

It's as if the water jets never get inside a glass or to the top 3rd rack at all. Samsung has sent repair persons out multiple times. Nearly every part of this machine has been replaced. It still doesn't clean. Samsung tried to tell me that my hot water has to be at LEAST 120 degrees for cycle to be effective, as there is no heating element in the unit. I pointed out there HAS to be a heating element in the unit because it has a SANITIZE cycle. Then they told me the problem was with my tankless water heater because a tankless heater requires several seconds of "draw" before kicking in, and then it takes 20-30 seconds to draw the hot water up from the unit in the basement. Because the dishwasher does not use a lot of water, it stops drawing water before the hot water gets to the unit. Ugh. Let's move on, cause there is more bad news. Flaw #1: The middle rack has 2 settings: high and low. If it is set to high, there is not enough height to put even a short wine glass in the 2nd rack. It's OK for most plain mugs and glasses, but oversized mugs, small dishes, lids, and plasticware either don't fit at all, or they take up 2 rows. Flaw #3: the many of the tines in the 2nd rack are spaced so far apart, that small lids or dishes consistently fall through. Flaw #4: Spacing of tines on bottom rack are also off. Pics on the Samsung website show plates in each slot, but customer service told me I had to skip every other slot so that water could get through. Huh? So I can only fill it halfway? Just in case you were wondering, it STILL doesn't clean when I skip every other slot. Every single time I look at that stupid $1k appliance, I get angry and regret the purchase. Worst money I have EVER spent on an appliance. Will NEVER buy Samsung again.

Sentence (English): The LG STUDIO 24 in.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher with a lot of features not included in other makes. ] || ---------------- || The LG STUDIO 24 in. PrintProof Stainless Steel Top Control Smart Dishwasher with 1-Hour Wash and Dry and TrueSteam is a really nicely built dishwasher. It is super quiet and will do all your dishes in only 1 hour. All the controls are on the top of the stainless steel door, easy to read and access. As quoted from the LG documentation: “LG dishwashers are certified by the National Sanitation Foundation to reduce bacteria on dishes by 99.999% and reach a final rinse temperature greater than 150°F when operated on the Steam cycle for peace of mind.” The racks are height adjustable to accommodate different sized dishes and pans. There are also 2 interior LED lights that come on when the door is opened to help you see your dishes. The interior is also made of stainless steel – not all that plastic stuff you see in other dishwashers. LG advertises that this dishwasher has high-pressure jets with 38% more cleaning power, sprays dishes from multiple angles while soaking them with over one million microbubbles to help break down stubborn food residue and provide exceptional cleaning performance. LG also has a built-in self-diagnosis system that informs you should something go wrong with the appliance. LG backs the motor with a 10-year warranty and a 2-year warranty overall. The dishwasher measures 33-5/8 inches high x 23-3/4 inches wide x 24-5/8 inches deep, so be sure the location you intend to install it in will accommodate the unit. The unit can be installed directly to a power source or an extra plug/cord can be purchased to plug the unit into an outlet. I had it installed by Home Depot and recommend that you have it installed. It only took less than an hour but you need to remove your old unit first. Also be sure you can turn off the water to the unit from under the sink and that the shutoff securely turns off the water – no drips. The Home Depot installers gave us a 4-hour window with progressive status reports of how many stops they have before arriving. That was very helpful. A very extensive Owner's Manual is also included in English, Spanish, and French. Overall, the dishwasher is extremely nice, well-built, nice looking, and quiet. I recommend it.

One of the features of the machine is that it is one of Bosch's quietest models (44dB), which is true in terms of the motor, since it is not audible, but the other natural noises (water jets on the dishes) are just as loud as in our previous machine, so essentially this is not a significant change brought. The plates, dishes and glasses are visibly cleaner than before, but according to my memories, the old machine was also able to produce this in its heyday. Which is a cool feature that opens the door after washing. What is disturbing is that a spring-loaded mechanism automatically pulls the door in. It's really annoying. I also don't like the fact that the trays wobble, it's much less stable than I would have imagined it to be, or what our previous machine was like. The installation instructions are of poor quality, it's practically hard to understand what needs to be done (so I'm an engineer). The Germans really messed this up, it doesn't work for them. The Wifi function that is included is practically unnecessary, I didn't use it much, but it is still more useful than the Wifi functionality of our Bosch smart refrigerator. :)
Comments (Original): [ Remek termék sok apró bakival ] || ---------------- || A vásárolt mosogatógép egy közép-felsőkategóriás gép sok extra funkcióval. A vásárlásának oka, hogy a korábbi (Gorenje márkájú) mosogatógép 12 év használat után elromlott. A gép egyik tulajdonsága, hogy a Bosch egyik leghalkabb modellje (44dB), ami a motort tekintve igaz, hiszen az nem hallható viszont az egyéb természetes zajok (vízsugár az edényeken) ugyan olyan hangosak, mint a korábbi gépünkben, tehát lényegében érdemi változást ez nem hozott.A tányérok, edények és poharak láthatóan tisztábbak, mint korábban, de a régi gép is tudott emlékeim szerint ilyet produkálni fénykorában.Ami klassz funkció, hogy mosás után kinyitja az ajtót.Ami zavaró, hogy egy rugós mechanika automatán behúzza az ajtót. Iszonyatosan idegesítő.Az sem tetszik, hogy a tálcák nyeklenek, sokkal kevésbé stabil, mint amilyennek képzeltem volna, vagy amilyen a korábbi gépünk.A beszerelési útmutató gyenge minőségű, gyakorlatilag alig érthető mit kell csinálni (úgy hogy mérnök vagyok). Ezt nagyon elbaltázták a németek, nem rájuk vall.A Wifi funkció ami benne van gyakorlatilag felesleges, sok hasznát nem vettem, de így is egyel hasznosabb, mint a Bosch okos hűtőnk Wifis funkcionalitása. :)

Sentence (English): I received the dishwasher just two days after ordering it.
Comments (English): [ It's the best. ] || ---------------- || I received the dishwasher just two days after ordering it. I expected it to be big, but it feels even bigger than I thought. It probably feels that way because I had to leave some space behind it for the wiring work. I used to use an SK Magic 6-person model, but I stopped using it after moving. However, I decided to buy this one recently due to wrist pain. It seems to be shorter in height but deeper than the SK Magic model. Also, since it has a single tier, there is plenty of room to fit pots! The placement is a perfect match for our sink. I love that I can just slide everything right into the dishwasher without spilling a single drop of water from the sink! I was going to buy a built-in model, but I don't like bending over, and unless guests come over, we don't have that much to wash, so I bought the 6-person model, and this is big enough. It is large enough to easily handle a meal for a family of four. I ran it on the standard mode; it didn't dry completely without a drop of water, and there were still some beading, but after opening the door, pulling out the shelf, and letting it sit for a while, it dried quickly, perhaps due to the heat. One minor drawback is that I wish there was a transparent window on the tempered glass front panel! I'm curious because I can't see the washing process. Another thing is the color of the drain pipe. How great would it have been if the drain pipe were white, too? The drain and water supply pipes are a bit unsightly, but I guess I have to put up with that. The water supply pipe requires drilling a hole in the sink countertop, but I didn't want to, so I finished it by tucking it into the gap between the countertop and the base cabinet. It doesn't look great aesthetically, but it's better than drilling a hole. I only used a quarter of a solid detergent, but the dishes came out spotlessly clean. They were greasy plates, but they came out sparkling clean—I am extremely satisfied. The design is beautiful, as expected from Bespoke, and the Samsung installers were very kind and installed it quickly. Hesitating only delays the delivery~
