Comments (English): [ Totally regret buying this, trust the bad reviews. ] || ---------------- || We bought this as a replacement when the basic GE machine that we had used for 17 years started leaking from the bottom. We figured that since our dishwasher was so old that we should just replace it instead of attempting to repair it. I thought that this machine would be a good replacement since the one we had before was pretty basic and this one has thousands of good reviews. I was a little reluctant to get this because of the bad reviews, but since most of them sounded like they either got a lemon, or they were complaining about the drying function(which I couldn't care less about), I thought this would work just fine for us. I was very wrong! This machine feels so much smaller on the inside than our previous machine(which is confusing because it is literally the same size), and can fit way less dishes in it since the racks are laid out so awkwardly. It is VERY loud, which was surprising to me because so many people in the reviews commented on how quiet it is. It sounds like a loud thunderstorm in our kitchen when it's running. Also, the cycle times are ridiculously long! It states that it has an hour cycle, which is true, but once you get it, the instructions make it clear that the hour cycle is just like a quick, not so great wash. But all these things aside, it doesn't wash well at all. If it at least did a good job, I could overlook the annoying things, and not leave a bad review. I was shocked to see that after running for HOURS and also having not just a detergent pod, but also a dishwasher cleaning pod(since I wanted it to be extra cleaned out since it was the first use), that there were dishes that were visibly dirty! And I should also point out that my dishes are already like 90-95% clean when I put them in the dishwasher. I am not one of those people who just knock off the big food chunks and throw stuff in the dishwasher. Everything is rinsed and presoaked/scrubbed if it has anything like cheese, egg, etc. stuck on. So, the dishwasher shouldn't even have to work very hard to get my dishes clean and it STILL did a terrible job. If it wouldn't be such a pain to go through the trouble of returning this, it would be going back tomorrow. I just wanted to warn other people so you don't make the same mistake I did. Trust the bad reviews, I don't understand how in the world this thing has good reviews.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher looks great and for now is working great (one month of use).
Comments (English): [ No Drying Option with Express Cycle ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher looks great and for now is working great (one month of use). My complaint is that the Express washing option does not have a dry cycle. The manual says "For better drying, select Dry or Ultra Dry." Well, you can't. I contacted GE and they walked me through a couple of arcane button-pushing combinations, but to no avail. They finally concluded that this model does not dry its Express cycle. I scoured the internet and was unable to find any solution. I really could have used the Express option, because we packed up all our dishes prior to our kitchen renovation and then wanted to wash them before putting them in the new cabinets. Had to use a normal cycle for every load, which felt very wasteful. The drying option is essential because on the first load that I tried I just hit the Express button and let 'er rip. When I opened the dishwasher at the end everything was SOAKED. Not "Just a little wet, so I'll put the glasses on a drying mat for a few minutes" wet, but BIBLICAL wet. I would have had to dry everything by hand, or let it sit for an hour or so while it air-dried. I'm the type of person who reads the manual even before I buy something, so this was a disappointment.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher does a good job cleaning my dishes and runs very quietly.
Comments (English): [ Doesn't Dry or Vent properly, but is pretty quiet. ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher does a good job cleaning my dishes and runs very quietly. However, it doesn't dry or vent properly. Whether I use a normal heated drying cycle or extended cycle, the entire inside of the dishwasher is wet and steamy at the end of a cycle. And overall the inside is always humid. We use a drying agent, and run the dishwasher with hot water. I believe the issue is that the dryer vent door should stay open longer during or after the drying cycle. Additionally when opening the door after running a cycle, water drips from the vent. So I have to clean that up from my floor after each load of dishes. I probably should have returned this after noticing these issues, however I have arranged a call with KA so that they will come try to repair it.

Comments (English): [ I always feel that LG is the best when it comes to home appliances ] || ---------------- || I ordered an LG built-in unit, but it was eventually deemed uninstallable. Since there was no other option for a countertop, I ordered this one reluctantly. First off, I used a liquid detergent that cleans squeaky clean; even with just 5mm of detergent, it was a sea of foam with HC floating on top. The plate shown in the picture was the one I used to hold only fried shrimp. After many trials and errors, I saw multiple times that it wasn't cleaning properly. This is the result of finally using a powerful Samsung-specific detergent and putting just that one plate of shrimp in. When it comes to home appliances, LG really is the best. I realized it painfully again this time. But the LG countertop is even worse. Let's stick to built-in appliances.

Sentence (English): I had this dishwasher 7 years.
Comments (English): [ Looks good but that was about it. ] || ---------------- || I had this dishwasher 7 years. It started leaking at 1 year and 3 days. GE wouldn't do anything about it since it was 3 days past the warranty. So I had to put pans under the front door every time I ran it. It worked great for a while besides the top rack rusting so bad within 2 years. I ordered a new rack since it was cheaper than a new unit. Then it worked ok until one day it wouldn't drain. Since this one leaked anyways, I purchased the 650 model and it literally worked for 1 hour, only 1 hour! Ran the 1 hour cycle as a test run. After that, it beeped 3 times and died and never turned on again. It had been installed for literally for that 1 hour cycle. Never owned a dishwasher for less than 1 day. Thankfully it was picked up but now I have to buy another unit and wait yet again. Honestly if people want to go green, these manufacturers need to make a quality product. 2 dishwashers from the same house headed to the dump within 1 day. Come on GE, do better. Have some pride and integrity for crying out loud! Make a product that people can't wait to own and be happy with for decades. There's your "go green" solution! Do. Better. GE. We all know you can since you used to be a great company.

Sentence (English): Don't be misled into thinking this is a true 500 Series Bosch.
Comments (English): [ Closer to an Upgraded 300 Rather than a 500 Series ] || ---------------- || Don't be misled into thinking this is a true 500 Series Bosch. It is not. It is basically an upgraded 300 Series where an adjustable 3rd rack replaces the standard (fixed) 3rd rack found on some 300 Series models. All other features and specifications are identical to the 300 Series - with the key missing 500 features being a lower sound rating (46 versus 44 dBA) and drying options ("Extra Dry" versus "AutoAir", which is a distinct 500 Series feature in the US). In my opinion, not worth the extra $200 ( at the time of this writing) over the identically spec'd 300 Series model SHE53C85N. Besides aesthetics, the only difference between the two models is the 3rd rack design ("Standard" vs "Flexible"). If you thought you were buying a quieter machine with the condensation releasing AutoAir feature, you'll be disappointed.

Comments (English): [Advantages] Easy to install. Just put it on the sink and plug it in. It washes cleanly and dries well. I'm so happy to be freed from the hassle of washing dishes. If you want to supply water automatically, you have to drill a hole in the sink. The tenant cries. You have to put water in manually, but it is not that cumbersome. There is a 1.8L water tank and a water tray?, so you can put it in easily. An alarm will sound when you put it in.
Comments (Original): [장점] ⭕️ 설치가 간편해요. 싱크대 위에 올려두고 전선만 꽂으면 돼요  ⭕️ 깨끗하게 세척되고 건조도 잘돼요. 설거지의 귀찮음에서 해방돼서 넘 기뻐요. 큰 건더기만 제거하고 식기세척기에 넣어요  ⭕️ 생각보다 많이 들어가요. 1인 가구 기준 세 끼 정도는 충분히 커버 가능해요. ⭕️ 디자인이 예뻐요. 흰색 & 블랙 조합이 예쁘네요. 두는 것만으로 주방이 세련되보여요  ⭕️ 물 빠짐 호스가 길어서 설치하기 편해요 --------------------------------------- [아쉬운 점] ✔️ 드럼 세탁기 정도의 소리에요. 예민하신 분들은 자는 곳 근처에 두고 쓸 수는 없을 것 같아요. 저는 개인적으로 상관 없었어요. ✔️ 문을 약간 열 수는 없어요  건조할 때 문이 자동으로 열리거나 중간 정도 열리면 좋을 텐데 아예 확 열거나 닫는 수 밖에 없네요. 공간 차지를 많이 해서 그 점이 약간 아쉽네요  ✔️ 사이즈가 생각보다 커요  500ML 물병이랑 비교해보면 상당히 크죠. 특히 깊이가 정말 깊어요. 오른쪽 공간 확보까지 고려하면 더 큰 공간이 필요해요. 원룸용... 으로 쓰기에는 좀 큰 거 같아요 ✔️ 급수 펌프 설치는 사실상 불가능해요. 수동이라고 봐요해요. 자동으로 급수되게 하려면 싱크대에 구멍을 뚫어야 한다네요... 임차인은 웁니다... 수동으로 물을 넣어야 하는데 그렇게 번거롭지는 않아요. 1.8L물통과 물받이? 가 있어서 쉽게 넣을 수 있어요. 다 넣으면 알림이 울립니다

Comments (English): [ A 6 person dishwasher would be good enough ] || ---------------- || Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop 6-Place Dishwasher Review! I'm a mom of two with four years of experience managing a household. A dishwasher was a much-needed appliance, but the main reason I hesitated to buy one was that people around me insisted dishwashers had to be huge. This meant I would have to install a 12-place setting or larger model, which required creating space in the lower kitchen cabinets. After much deliberation regarding the increasing amount of housework, I purchased a 6-place setting dishwasher that can be installed without any construction work! My household consists of two adults and two children. Since the children are still young and the adults mainly eat delivery food or simple meal kits, we do generate a fair amount of dishes, but not as many as a large family. So, I decided to give the 6-place setting a try and bought it. The conclusion is: I am truly, extremely satisfied! I should have bought it sooner. The 6-place setting is more than sufficient for our household. Since I get the urge to wash dishes immediately when the sink fills up, it is great to be able to run the dishwasher whenever that happens. I have a bad back, so I liked being able to load dishes without bending over. Even the 6-place setting fits a lot more than I expected. You can easily run pots and pans along with the dishes. The noise isn't that loud either! In fact, I actually like the sound of the dishwasher running. The thought that housework has decreased, allowing me to organize other things or have some free time, has significantly reduced my stress. Moreover, the price of the Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher was really affordable. I can honestly say this is one of the most satisfying purchases I've made this year. For those who found the price or installation space of 12-place setting or larger dishwashers too burdensome, I would recommend buying the 6-place setting like I did; it is more than sufficient for everyday use.

Sentence (English): We replaced the dishwasher that came with our house which is 40 years old, so we're not sure if it is original to the house, but it certainly is at least 20 years old.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher, no "holes" in cleaning radius ] || ---------------- || We replaced the dishwasher that came with our house which is 40 years old, so we're not sure if it is original to the house, but it certainly is at least 20 years old. Upgrading to this Bosch is a whole new world. No more holes where nothing gets clean in a gap, everything cleans, and it's so quiet! The baskets could use some improvement, as could the wine-glass holders (which I use for other uses), and I wish there were more configurations for the bottom rack, but being that this is a basic model and the upgrades have these features, we're not too upset. I do wish there was some sort of monitoring system so we could know where in the cycle it was though. It just shows how many hours left (and I can't believe a load takes over 2 hours now, when our old one took just over 1 hr). Filter removes and cleans really easily. Sometimes the walls are still wet, but all the dishes are dry so that's fine, and so far no musty smell. Time will tell how long the latch holds up though - strange that there is no manual latch, you just have to tug on it to open the auto latch, and it gets opened and closed several times a day since I don't keep the door open.

Turns out GE quietly dropped the disposer from this model 10 months ago and never updated their online specifications. With this much of a drastic change the model should have been completely phased out and new information with a new model number and description put out there. Very disappointed. Now I'm stuck with it. Lowes made a partial refund but doesn't cover the time I wasted researching and they said they had no other model with a disposer to replace it. This was my first and probably last GE appliance.
